newsitem.title: USA: U.S. has no plan for mass expulsion of Nicaraguans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. has no plan for mass expulsion of Nicaraguans.

text.p: The United States assured Nicaragua on Thursday that it planned no mass deportation of illegal Nicaraguan immigrants and each case would be examined individually on its merits.

Nicaraguan Foreign Minister Emilio Alvarez said on Wednesday he would urge U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to delay what Managua fears could be a mass expulsion of an estimated 40,000 such immigrants.
"We are aware of the Nicaraguan government's concerns about absorbing large numbers of deportees," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
"We have assured the Nicaraguan government that each of these cases will be examined individually. There will be no mass deportations," he told reporters.
Burns said "compassion will be balanced with respect for United States government immigration law" when cases were reviewed by the Immigration and Naturalisation Service.
The U.S. spokesman noted that many of the immigrants had arrived in the 1980s when Nicaragua was gripped by civil war.
Alvarez said he would ask Albright during a meeting with other Central American foreign ministers in Washington on April 2 to delay the expulsions.

He said a recent change in U.S. immigration law meant that Nicaraguans with less than seven years residence in the United States who have received deportation orders can no longer appeal. He expected the deportations to start July 16.
"We are asking that they push back this date," Alvarez told a news conference in Managua.
